answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable bond before it can trade. Like a juniper hedge that is cheap to plant once but costly to grow everywhere, one bond is affordable while a thousand fake accounts drain an attacker's funds. Honest work slowly returns the bond, and peers can vote to slash it for fraud, so a summit of trusted agents stays clean while ivory-tower fakes priced out of the market simply cannot afford to appear.
